It has three panels: one wide panel on top, then two tall panels below, left and right. Panel 1 (top): I read the caption at top left first, 'Soon, his slot comes up.' My eye then moves right to the teal label at top right, 'NOW · A-12'. There is a small placeholder labelled ravi at upper centre-right and a smaller one labelled meera at the far right below the label. Neither speaks, so they are silent presences. pages.observation: The order is clear. In each panel the caption sits at top left, so nothing competes for the first read. In panel 1, the 'NOW · A-12' label is far from the caption and lies on the same top line, so it is read second. That works, but who or what displays it (screen, ticket) cannot be told from the placeholder. In panel 1, ravi and meera have no dialogue, and meera is a tiny box at the right edge; her presence and role are not established on this page. In panel 2, the nurse's balloon sits right above the nurse box and the tail is short and correct. Ravi's box (lower left) is far from the balloon and gives no reply, which reads as silent compliance; no reply seems to be skipped. In panel 3, the caption and the 'RAVI · READY' label are far apart, with a large empty area around the ananya box. The label is read last as the panel's exit, which works, but its link to Ananya (is she seeing a notification?) depends on the artwork. No text overlaps a placeholder face box, and I found no hard-to-read text. Panels 2 and 3 are very tall with much empty space; check this in the artwork stage. This is a placeholder storyboard, so I could not judge whether lettering will cover real faces or hands.

pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png with Read and looked at it myself. It has four panels: wide top, wide middle, then two bottom panels left and right. Panel 1 (top): the speech balloon at top centre comes first, with its tail to the ananya placeholder on its left: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' The ravi placeholder at the right is silent. Then the large teal label at middle left: 'PATIENT DETAILS: current vitals · prior health info · allergy panel · AI mic option · patient docs · lab reports'. Panel 2 (middle): left balloon, tail to ananya: 'May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?' Middle balloon, long tail running down-right to ravi: 'Yes, I agree.' Teal label at right: 'AI VOICE CONSENT: asked at the first visit, before any voice is saved'. Panel 3 (bottom left): balloon at top left, tail to the ravi placeholder on the right: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' Then the large teal label at lower left: 'SOAP NOTES: fill in manually and choose ICD or SNOMED codes, or let AI listen and summarise the conversation'. Panel 4 (bottom right): caption at top: 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The ananya placeholder is centre and silent. A ravi marker dot sits at the far right edge with no box, also silent. Natural order: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' -> 'PATIENT DETAILS: ...' -> 'May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?' -> 'Yes, I agree.' -> 'AI VOICE CONSENT: ...' -> 'I've been feeling tired lately.' -> 'SOAP NOTES: ...' -> 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.'
pages.observation: 1) Panel 1 has a first-entry ambiguity. The PATIENT DETAILS label is at the far left but lower; the balloon is higher but centred. Most readers will read the balloon first because it is higher, but some may start at the large left label. The label is long (six items) and dominates the panel. 2) The reply to Ananya's question 'Tell me what brings you in.' is delayed. The consent exchange in panel 2 comes between them, and Ravi's answer 'I've been feeling tired lately.' only arrives in panel 3. Read in order it still makes sense (a consent check, then the answer), but the gap means 'I've been feeling tired lately.' is two balloons away from the question it answers. Check whether this is intended or whether a reader might think the answer is to the consent question. 3) In panel 2, the 'Yes, I agree.' balloon sits close to Ananya's balloon, almost touching. Its tail is long and runs diagonally across the panel to ravi, passing very close to (and appearing to graze) the bottom-left corner of the AI VOICE CONSENT label. Reading both balloons together is natural, so no reply is skipped, but the tail and label crowding should be fixed. The consent label, read after the answer, works as an explanation, but it is read after the fact. 4) In panel 3, the balloon tail correctly reaches the ravi box. The SOAP NOTES label is very long, eight lines, and takes up much of the panel's lower half. It is readable, but heavy. 5) In panel 4, the ravi marker has only a dot at the right panel edge and no face box. If Ravi is visible, his face position is not marked; if he is off-panel, the marker is misleading. The caption is narration, and no speech is skipped. 6) No balloon or label overlaps a placeholder face box, apart from the panel 2 tail running near the label. I found no illegible text. I could not judge real faces, hands or objects from placeholders.

A long teal title label at top reads 'SPECIALITY-SPECIFIC TREATMENT PLANNER'. Below it, three teal labels run left to right: 'Dentist: odontogram', then 'Eye doctor: eye markers', then 'Paediatrician: growth scales · vaccines'. Panel 2 (bottom): a speech balloon at top centre comes first, its tail pointing down-left to the ananya placeholder: 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' The ravi placeholder at the right is silent, a listening reaction. Then the teal label at lower left: 'PLAN OF CARE: intelligent prescribing · summary · drug interactions · labs · referrals'. Natural order: 'SPECIALITY-SPECIFIC TREATMENT PLANNER' -> 'Dentist: odontogram' -> 'Eye doctor: eye markers' -> 'Paediatrician: growth scales · vaccines' -> 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' -> 'PLAN OF CARE: intelligent prescribing · summary · drug interactions · labs · referrals'.
pages.observation: Panel 1 has no person and no balloon. It reads as a screen or feature diagram, and the left-to-right order of the three specialty labels is clear. The 'Eye doctor' and 'Paediatrician' labels nearly touch, while there is a wider gap between 'Dentist' and 'Eye doctor'. The spacing is uneven, but this does not cause misreading. A large blank area lies between the title and the three labels. Who is looking at this planner, and how it connects to the previous scene, cannot be told from this page. In panel 2, the balloon tail correctly reaches the ananya box. Ravi gives no spoken reply to 'together', so his reaction must come from the art. That is a possible gap if a verbal or visible agreement is expected. The PLAN OF CARE label sits at lower left, below and left of the characters. Read left to right and top to bottom, it comes after the balloon. But because it is at the far left, some readers may jump to it before the balloon or treat it as separate from the dialogue. Its link to the speech (a plan being formed) is implied only by the label. No text overlaps a placeholder face box, and I found no hard-to-read text. I could not judge real faces, hands or objects from placeholders.
